subject: DPA: erase-notice window, backup retention SLA, and lawful-access carveouts
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on DPA erase/certification flow

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to legal review I need to confirm a few DPA items related to erase and residency:

- What is Redwood's operational definition of an "erase request"? We need a clear SLA for completion and a signed certificate of deletion.
- How long are snapshots/backups retained after an erase is executed? Our policy requires proof that backups are handled.
- In the event of lawful requests (subpoena, warrant), how will customer data be handled and what notice, if any, will we receive?

Attached: Aurelia-DPA-questions.pdf (list of checklist items from Aurelia legal).

Can you send suggested DPA language or a short playbook we can circulate with our counsel?

Best,
Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Security & Privacy
Aurelia Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@aureliahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA erase/certification flow

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the detailed checklist. High-level proposal from our side (draft language follows):

1) Operational erase definition and SLA
- "Erase request" = removal of all customer-identifying production data from live serving systems and primary storage.
- SLA: Redwood will complete production data erasure and provide a certificate of deletion within 30 calendar days of an authorized request for hosted customers.

2) Backups and snapshots
- Backups: immutable backups and snapshots retained for operational recovery for 45 days by default, then pruned. Backups are encrypted and stored in region.
- For erase requests, Redwood will expunge corresponding keys and mark snapshots for destruction; physical deletion from backup media will follow normal retention/garbage-collection cycles (up to 45 days) unless a shorter retention is contractually agreed.

3) Lawful access / notice
- Redwood will provide notice of lawful requests to the extent permitted by law. Where notice is prohibited, we will notify customer as soon as legally possible and provide redacted support logs/audit entries demonstrating limited scope.

4) Evidence and certification
- Certificate will include timestamped audit of erase operations and a signed statement of scope. We can offer additional third-party attestation as an enterprise add-on.

I attached a short playbook (redwood-erase-playbook-v1.pdf) that maps steps, owners, and artifacts we can provide to customers and auditors.

If Aurelia's counsel needs alternative wording (e.g., shorter proof windows or a different backup retention) we can propose contractual carveouts or an addendum for private deployments.

Looping in Rishi (sec) and Laura (legal) for any immediate redlines.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-03T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA erase/certification flow

Thanks for the clear start. A few suggested technical clarifications for the DPA wording (so legal doesn't interpret backup lifecycle as indefinite):

> Backups: immutable backups and snapshots retained for operational recovery for 45 days by default, then pruned.

Can we change to: "Backups and immutable snapshots will be retained for a maximum of 45 days following creation; where an erase request is received, Redwood will mark any affected snapshots for expedited deletion and will remove access by destroying the encryption keys within the standard 45-day window, subject to lawful-hold exceptions."

Also recommend adding an explicit lawful-hold process in the playbook:
- Customer can provide a signed legal-hold notice to Redwood legal@redwood.ai. Redwood will cease scheduled destruction and preserve relevant materials for the specified scope.
- Redwood will supply audit logs showing hold start/end and affected artifacts.

If Aurelia needs a 30-day backup retention instead of 45 we can entertain that as a commercial concession, but it will change the deletion SLA.

- Rishi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@aureliahealth.com>, Harper Legal LLP <privacy@harperlegal.com>
Date: 2028-11-05T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA erase/certification flow

Stephanie / Rishi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Aurelia's legal has reviewed and has a counterproposal: they want a faster certificate/notice window and shorter backup exposure. Key asks:

- Erase certificate: completion and signed certificate within 10 business days for hosted customers (Aurelia says this is necessary for compliance with their internal data minimization policy).
- Backups: 30-day max retention for snapshots/backups; for any affected records Redwood to remove access and certify key destruction within 7 business days.
- Lawful access: Aurelia requests "prior notice" for any non-emergency lawful access where permitted by law.

Attached: Aurelia-redlines.docx (their proposed DPA redline).

Two notes from counsel: 1) they are open to a compromise where the hosted-service deletion SLA is 14 business days if Redwood can commit to a 30-day backup retention; 2) they asked whether private deployment (VPC/on-prem) can be offered with a 7-business-day certificate.

Can your team confirm operationally whether 7/10 business days is feasible or provide a standard compromise we can present to counsel?

—Maya

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-08T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA erase/certification flow

Maya / Daniel / Harper Legal —

Thanks — good visibility into Aurelia's constraints. After internal ops + security + legal discussion here is a pragmatic path we can commit to and propose as DPA language:

- Hosted customers: Redwood will complete production-data erasure and provide a signed certificate within 14 business days of an authenticated erase request. This certificate will include a scoped audit of storage locations, timestamps, and the role that executed the deletion.
- Backup retention: Default 30-day retention for immutable snapshots/backups. For affected records identified in an erase request, Redwood will remove access by destroying encryption keys within 7 business days and will include key-destruction metadata in the deletion certificate. Physical media purging will follow natural garbage-collection cycles but will not exceed 45 days.
- Private/On-prem offering: For customers requiring faster proof (7 business days for full certificate), we can offer a private deployment addendum with the accelerated SLA and additional operational controls (customer-managed keys, local-only snapshots).
- Lawful access: Redwood will provide notice unless prohibited by law; where notice is prohibited, Redwood will provide post-event disclosure as permitted and a redacted record of requester scope. We will also accept customer-initiated legal-hold notices to pause destruction schedules; those holds will be logged and visible in the customer console.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Laura to draft the DPA excerpt reflecting the above (I attached final-dpa-excerpt.txt as a working seed).
2) Rishi & Priyom to add the technical appendix for key-destruction proof and audit log format.
3) Stephanie to provide a commercial note: the 30-day default retention and 14 business-day certificate are standard for our hosted plan; 7-business-day certificates require private deployment or a one-time services fee.

If Aurelia agrees in principle we'll route Laura's draft to Harper Legal for a quick redline pass and then circulate for signature via DocuSign.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachments: final-dpa-excerpt.txt
DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/embedded/sign/abc123-erase-addendum
